activities.anchor: The foundational scheme is three roles
activities.caption: file each job under the role that does it
activities.name: cinRolesBuckets

config.prompt: Three roles, not necessarily three lamps — file each job:

items.label: placed to read as the window or the lamp in the scene
lifts the shadow side — the style dial
usually a bounce board or the room's own walls, not a lamp
separates the subject from the background
the hair-light halo that reads as 'expensive' in interviews

config.why: Change the ratios and nothing changes but mood — the scheme is grammar; the ratios are the sentence.

activities.anchor: converting between and mixed temperatures used deliberately
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the physics shortlist
activities.name: cinTempCloze

config.text: Tungsten runs about %%0%% K (warm); daylight about %%1%% K (cool) — the warm interior against the blue window of a thousand night exteriors is two temperatures arguing. And the visible desk lamp is one of the %%2%% — the scheme's alibi while three hidden units do the work.
config.hint: Gels — CTO and CTB — convert between the two temperatures.

activities.caption: put the comedy on the ratio dial
activities.name: cinRatioPlace

config.prompt: Key-to-fill ratio, the genre signal — where does classic comedy and advertisement sit?
config.why: High-key — 2:1 or gentler — signals safety, comedy, advertisement; 8:1 and beyond signals threat, secrecy, moral murk. Audiences read genre from contrast instantly, before a word is spoken.

activities.anchor: The colour lesson's schemes become narrative systems
activities.caption: pair each film with its colour argument
activities.name: cinColourMatch

config.prompt: Four colour systems, four arguments — pair them:

pairs.right: warm skin against cool shadows — skin is the anchor audiences watch
three chapters of identity built from palette shifts
neon and venetian-blind shafts as a whole future's weather
Christmas amber bathing interiors that reads as ritual

config.why: Exposure is authorship too: what you choose to render as black and as white sets the image's moral range — nothing in the image is neutral.

items.label: Blade Runner 2049's detail in every black

config.why: Deep focus remains the historical hinge — Toland on Citizen Kane staged within the frame instead of cutting within it, a philosophy Wes Anderson and Deakins inherit.

activities.anchor: each support system is a rhetorical register
activities.caption: pair each support with the sentence it speaks
activities.name: cinSupportMatch

config.prompt: Five systems, five registers — pair them:

pairs.right: composure — locked-off frames, exact pans and tilts
cinema's original moving sentence — the slow push-in leans toward
the aerial establishing shot as utility, not helicopter-day expense

config.why: The support system is chosen for the sentence the shot speaks — composure, pursuit, sweep or shake; mis-matching register to meaning reads as production noise.

activities.caption: bet before you read on — the smoothness demand
activities.name: cinGimbalPredict

config.q: A producer demands every shot go on a stabiliser, because smoother footage is always more professional. What is the counter-argument?
choices: Stability is a register, not a virtue — that floating glide is wrong for panic and wrong for documentary honesty
Stabilisers are for amateurs; everything should be handheld
The producer is right — smoothness never hurts
config.why: A handheld tremor can be exactly the right instrument. The question is never 'how smooth' but 'which sentence does this movement speak'.

activities.caption: the three-week night interior — trace the defence
activities.name: cinContinuityBranch

config.root: A two-page night interior shoots across three weeks, on stages and locations, with weather intervening.

start.text: How does the look survive the shooting order?

choices.label: Rely on the DP's memory and a good eye
choices.feedback: Heroic — and exactly what the discipline replaced.

choices.label: Log every setup, keep reference stills, carry the grade intent on set
choices.feedback: The professional defence: procedural, not heroic.

choices.label: Let each day find its own look — that is realism
choices.feedback: The audience will feel what it cannot name.

heroic.text: Memory fails quietly: the sun changes sides between shots, a window goes from blue to amber — continuity-of-light failures the audience senses before it can name them.

procedure.text: Fixture, position, filtration, intensity — logged; reference stills kept; LUTs applied on set so every monitor shows the target look, not raw sensor output. Measure, log, photograph, replicate.

drift.text: Unless it is planned: as tension rises, slowly warming the key in both shots of a cut is authorship — unplanned drift reads as mistake.

config.why: The look is a system; systems are maintained or designed, never accidental.
